title: 赠花卿
author: 杜甫
intro: Music drifts all day over Chengdu, half on the river wind, half into the clouds. “Music like this belongs in heaven” — still the standard Chinese compliment for a beautiful performance.
analysis: 这首诗写音乐之美。花卿是成都的一位将军，叫花敬定。第一句写成都城里每天都有乐声，“丝管”指弦乐器和管乐器，“纷纷”写出乐声又多又热闹。第二句很有想象力：乐声一半随着江风飘走，一半飘进了云里。声音本来看不见，诗人却写得好像能看到它飞到哪里去。第三、四句是千古名句：这样的曲子只应该天上才有，人间能听到几回呢？今天中国人夸一首曲子、一段演奏特别好听，还常说“此曲只应天上有”。另外，历来有人认为这首诗是含蓄的讽刺：古代礼制规定，有些乐曲只有皇帝才能用，花敬定却随便使用，“天上”暗指皇宫。这样看，表面是夸奖，实际是提醒。两种读法都说得通。
analysisEn: On the surface this is a poem about beautiful music. Hua Qing was General Hua Jingding, stationed in Chengdu. The first line says that every day the city is full of the sound of strings and pipes. The second is wonderfully imaginative: half of the music floats off on the wind over the river, half rises into the clouds. Sound is invisible, but Du Fu makes us see where it goes. The last two lines are the famous ones: such tunes should exist only in heaven — how many times in this world can one hear them? Chinese people still use 此曲只应天上有 to praise a lovely song or performance. But there has long been another reading. In Tang times certain music was reserved for the emperor, and General Hua was notorious for overstepping his place. “Heaven” may quietly mean the imperial court — so the compliment could be a polite warning that he was using music he had no right to. Both readings work, and that double edge is part of the poem's charm.
background: Du Fu (712–770) wrote this around 761 in Chengdu. Hua Jingding was a general who had helped put down a local rebellion but was known for his arrogance; the idea that the poem is a veiled criticism goes back to Ming-dynasty commentators.
pronunciation: 此曲 qǔ；只应 zhǐ yīng（只应当）；人间 jiān；几回 jǐ；卿 qīng。
version: 采用通行教材版本。维基文库所收《全唐诗》本“只应”作“秪应”，“秪”同“只”，意思相同，网站用通行写法“只”。

lines.py: jǐn chéng sī guǎn rì fēn fēn
lines.lit: In the City of Brocade, strings and pipes daily, many and busy;
lines.en: All day the strings and pipes fill the City of Brocade;

lines.py: bàn rù jiāng fēng bàn rù yún
lines.lit: half goes into the river wind, half into the clouds.
lines.en: half the music drifts on the river wind, half floats into the clouds.

lines.py: cǐ qǔ zhǐ yīng tiān shàng yǒu
lines.lit: This tune should only exist in heaven;
lines.en: A tune like this belongs in heaven —

lines.py: rén jiān néng dé jǐ huí wén
lines.lit: in the human world, how many times can one hear it?
lines.en: how often does the world below get to hear it?

words.en: to give as a gift; to dedicate

words.note: “卿”是古代对人的尊称；现代汉语里不再这样称呼人。
“丝”指琴、琵琶等弦乐器，“管”指笛、箫等管乐器，合起来指音乐。
现代汉语常用，如“议论纷纷”“纷纷离开”。

words.py: cǐ qǔ zhǐ yīng tiān shàng yǒu
words.en: this tune belongs only in heaven
words.note: 今天仍常用来夸奖音乐特别美妙。“曲”读 qǔ，是乐曲。
和“天上”相对，现代汉语也常用。
古义是听见；现代汉语“闻”多指用鼻子闻。

imagery.name: 风
imagery.zh: 江风把乐声带走，让看不见的音乐好像有了方向和形状。
imagery.en: The river wind carries the music off, giving invisible sound a direction and a shape.

imagery.name: 云
imagery.zh: 乐声飘进云里，暗示它高妙得像天上的仙乐。
imagery.en: Music rising into the clouds suggests it is as lofty as the music of heaven.
